content.comment_body: One of my clients has a [product_name] with [article_no]. When the Ethernet cable is disconnected, the controller shows an 'urgent message'. I haven't been able to reproduce this issue in my office environment. Is it possible to detect this in the logic design? It seems that 'OK' must be pressed to acknowledge the message, regardless of whether the cable is reconnected. Is there a way to bypass this acknowledgment?

The displayed message is: Urgent Event - Network Error. If this message appears when disconnecting the Ethernet cable, it's because the diagnostic indicator is active. These alerts can only be cleared by pressing OK. If you prefer not to see this message: navigate to Main Menu > Diagnostics > Toggle > Select 'Toggle event' and set it to disable.
That's exactly what I needed, thank you!

analysis.insight_summary: Users note that disconnecting the Ethernet cable from the [product_name] (with [article_no]) triggers an urgent message that always requires manual acknowledgment. This is linked to a diagnostic setting—when enabled, the event cannot be bypassed and needs confirmation with 'OK'. Users find it challenging to replicate the behavior and seek to automate or disable this acknowledgment, but the system defaults to requiring manual interaction.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to identify and ideally disable or bypass the need to manually acknowledge urgent network error messages when the Ethernet cable is unplugged.
